long_biography.plain_text:
In 1990, Angeliki Frangou borrowed $1.5 million from her shipowner father to buy the disabled freighter Fulvia in Brazil. She restored it, returned it to service and used the venture to build Franser, later combining that company with Maritime Enterprises Management. The sequence paired a fifth-generation shipping upbringing with the analytical discipline she developed through mechanical-engineering studies and early work on Wall Street.

Frangou made her defining corporate move in 2005, when the special-purpose acquisition company she led bought the established Navios dry-bulk business. She used public capital and acquisitions to expand Navios across dry bulk, containers, tankers and South American logistics. She remains chairwoman and chief executive of Navios Maritime Partners, where her strategy emphasizes diversified vessels, contracted employment and financial discipline through shipping cycles.
